requirements.evidence: All endpoints and contract details are implemented: routes/api.php:7-12 (throttle:10,1 on auth, throttle:30,1 on ticket, totem.auth group); 400/401 pairing paths in TotemAuthController.php:20-28 and :37-43; the transaction with lockForUpdate plus consume, create totem and sign JWT with all required claims at TotemAuthController.php:30-71; the 200 payload includes the entity pair at :87-95. The middleware covers every 401 case, the entity cross-check and the claim ∩ current-join scope (TotemAuth.php:31-79). The controller handles 403 forbidden, 404 queue_not_found scoped by entity_id, 422 inactive_queue and 422 invalid_priority, and issues tickets through IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TotemQueueController.php:20-161). bootstrap/app.php:31-37 renders rate_limited. CORS uses patterns for localhost/127.0.0.1 plus TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN with supports_credentials=false (config/cors.php). phpunit.xml pins the secret and TTL, .env.example has both keys, and the three docs are updated. Small gaps: TotemPairingCode.php:28-34 does not handle a random code colliding with another preset's unique login_code (the DB would throw), and 'description' is hardcoded to null.

conventions.evidence: Issuance reuses App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemQueueController.php:155). The models declare #[Fillable] deliberately. All three migrations have a reversible down(). Docs (docs/api/totem.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md) and CHANGELOG.md are kept in sync. Deviations: input checks are hand-rolled (TotemAuthController.php:19-28, TotemQueueController.php:146-150) instead of $request->validate (defensible because of the custom error codes). Scope authorization lives in private controller helpers rather than a policy or gate. New ad-hoc namespaces App\Support and App\Totem are introduced. The public controller methods have no return types or PHPDoc.

security.evidence: Signature comparison is constant-time (hash_equals, TotemJwt.php:64), the algorithm is pinned to HS256 (:58) and expiry is checked (:74). Every call re-validates totem, preset and entity (TotemAuth.php:47-69). Queues are resolved within the entity only (TotemQueueController.php:42-45). The pairing response gives no oracle, the code is never logged, and CORS sends no credentials. Gap: TotemJwt::encode refuses an empty secret (:26), but decode does not. If TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is unset, TotemAuth calls decode with '' (TotemAuth.php:39), so tokens HMAC'd with an empty key are accepted. The ids involved are sequential and guessable. The 32-character minimum is also not enforced.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TotemApiTest.php has 19 Pest tests. They cover the pairing command (success and unknown preset), the 400 formats including empty, the 401 no-oracle cases (unknown, expired, consumed, inactive), pairing claims and single use, the 429 rate_limited response, and expired, tampered and wrong-secret tokens. They also cover inactive totem and preset, entity mismatch with 403, immediate scope removal, a foreign or unknown queue returning 404 and an unscoped one 403, priorities, sequential A001/A002 with channel totem, invalid_priority and inactive_queue creating nothing, and CORS allow/deny plus preflight. Missing: last_seen_at update, a correctly signed token with mismatched entity/totem/preset claims, a 10-minute expiry assertion and printed output for the command, audit log assertions, the ticket throttle at 30/min, and TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN.

simplicity.evidence: The small HS256 implementation is allowed by the task and keeps dependencies out. The queues, priorities and issue endpoints share their resolution helpers. Some duplication: TotemPriorities::values() hardcodes [0, 10, 20] separately from all() (TotemPriorities.php:39-42), so the 'single source' can drift. Issue checks the inactive queue itself and also catches InactiveQueueException (TotemQueueController.php:141-159), duplicating the action's rule. The redundant $queueModel->fresh() costs an extra query. The catch-all Route::options('/{any}') (routes/api.php:14) duplicates what the CORS middleware already does.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the middleware docblock explains the scope rule (TotemAuth.php:20-31). The resolveQueue array-shape return ('error'/'status' vs 'queue', TotemQueueController.php:37-56) is awkward. The auth transaction returns a positional tuple [$totem, $preset->id, $entity, $token, $ttl] (TotemAuthController.php:71,80). There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. The extras are the unused 'web_origin' key in config/services.php:839, which config/cors.php reads via env() instead, and the global OPTIONS catch-all route (routes/api.php:14).

issues.explanation: decode() accepts an empty secret, unlike encode(). With TOTEM_JWT_SECRET unset, anyone can forge a valid token by HMAC-signing guessable sequential ids with an empty key. Fail closed instead, and enforce the 32-character minimum.
A random code that collides with another preset's unique login_code makes save() throw a unique-constraint error instead of retrying.
values() hardcodes [0, 10, 20] separately from all(), so the 'single source' of priorities can drift. Derive it from all().

Missing tests: last_seen_at update, a validly signed token with mismatched entity/totem/preset claims, the 10-minute expiry and printed code from the command, audit logging, the 30/min issuance throttle, and TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN.
Entity and queue scope authorization is hand-rolled in private controller helpers instead of a policy or gate, and input checks bypass $request->validate.
The inactive check is duplicated: the controller checks it and also catches the action's InactiveQueueException, plus an unnecessary $queueModel->fresh() query.
The catch-all OPTIONS route duplicates the CORS middleware's preflight handling, and services.totem.web_origin is never read.
The transaction returns a positional tuple, and resolveQueue returns an error/queue array union. Both are harder to follow than early responses or small value objects.

review.summary: The change adds the totem pairing command, JWT pairing endpoint, auth middleware, the three scoped endpoints (reusing IssueTicket), CORS config, migrations, models, factories, docs and a broad Pest suite, and closely matches the contract. One security gap holds it back from approval as is: JWT decode accepts an empty secret, so a missing TOTEM_JWT_SECRET allows forged tokens. The rest are minor items: duplicated priority values, an unhandled pairing-code collision, and a few untested paths. Approvable once the empty-secret check is fixed.
